themes.theme: Reverse DCF and Conservative Growth Estimates

positions.commentary: The speaker mentions that people have asked Warren Buffett how he conceives his DCF, noting he lowers cash flow amounts until comfortable, similar to assuming Apple generates less cash flow.

thesis: The episode argues that investors should prioritize confidence in conservative growth estimates (3-5%) over high-growth assumptions when evaluating Meta, noting that the company has returned to strong growth and margin expansion despite business challenges like ATT deprecating targeting. It suggests that if management is executing correctly on AI, a lower growth floor is acceptable, drawing a parallel to Warren Buffett's approach of lowering cash flow assumptions until comfortable.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests it is easier to have confidence in a conservative growth estimate for Meta (at least 3%) rather than a high one (20%+), implying a comfortable lower bound.
claims.quote: And so, again, the idea there is that it would be much easier to have confidence that meta is going to grow at least 3%, then say, oh, I think they're going to return to, you know, you know, 20% plus growth, have margin expansion.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Meta returned to 20% plus growth and margin expansion, which happened despite the need for confidence in a lower band of outcomes to make a decision.
claims.quote: And of course, that is what happened. But you didn't need to have confidence in this kind of high band of outcomes in order to make a decision at that time.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that a memo used Meta as a good example of reverse DCF inputs and outputs, noting the author looked smart as of October 15th, 2024.
claims.quote: And yeah, I loved, I loved in this memo how you kind of took exactly the snapshot of the inputs and the reverse DCF outputs of meta. And, you know, of course, it was a, it was a good example to use because as of October or 15th, 2024, you know, you look pretty smart, I have to say.
